findings.title: Invalid CSS property -webkit-align-items in align-items mixin
findings.body: The new align-items mixin emits `-webkit-align-items: $alignment;`. WebKit/Blink never shipped this property — they used `-webkit-box-align` for the 2009 spec (already included on line 118) and then went straight to the unprefixed `align-items`. The `-webkit-align-items` declaration is not a recognized CSS property; browsers will discard it silently. It clutters the compiled output and is a clear typo adjacent to the correct `-webkit-box-align` line.

findings.title: Invalid CSS property -ms-align-items in align-items mixin
findings.body: The new align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The IE 10 prefix for align-items is `-ms-flex-align` (already included on line 120); `-ms-align-items` is not a real CSS property. The redundant invalid declaration is silently ignored by browsers and is a typo. The correct line should be removed.

findings.title: Invalid CSS property -webkit-order in order mixin
findings.body: The new order mixin emits `-webkit-order: $val;`. WebKit/Blink never shipped this property — they used `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` for the 2009 spec (already included on line 126) and then went straight to the unprefixed `order`. `-webkit-order` is not a valid CSS property and is silently ignored. This is a typo adjacent to the correct `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` line.

findings.title: Removed bullet badge vertical alignment without replacement
findings.body: The diff deletes the rule `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper { float: left; &.bullet { margin-top: 5px; } }` and replaces it with `float: left` only, while also adding `@include order(2)` to the wrapper. The previous `margin-top: 5px` on bullet-style badges was used to vertically align the colored bullet with adjacent baseline-aligned text (a typical alignment fix for inline elements used inside a larger line of text). Nothing in this PR provides an equivalent offset, so bullet-style category badges rendered inside `.extra-info-wrapper` (e.g., on topic lists and the topic page header) may now sit visually lower than the surrounding text. This is a regression with no test or visual reference provided.

findings.title: Large padding reduction on .small-action-desc is untested
findings.body: `.small-action-desc` padding was changed from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` (with a matching `margin-top: 5px`) to `padding: 0 1.5%` while `.small-action` is converted to a flex container. The original 4em left padding was sized to clear the `.topic-avatar` icon column in the float-based layout. In the new flex layout the avatar becomes a sibling flex item, but the new `padding: 0 1.5%` collapses the inner `.avatar`'s surrounding space to a tiny percentage with no minimum, and the old `margin-top: 5px` was dropped without a replacement. Combined with the removal of `padding-top: 4px` on `> p`, the description block is likely to render noticeably tighter and/or vertically misaligned versus the avatar column. No screenshot, test, or visual regression coverage accompanies this change.

findings.title: Complete removal of .title rule while relying on flex container
findings.body: The diff deletes the entire `.title { float: left; }` rule and turns `.contents` into a flex container. While removing the float is intentional, the rule is now gone entirely — any other declaration (e.g., `min-width`, `max-width`, `flex` shrink behavior, `white-space`) that downstream consumers might have relied on for the title element is no longer being applied here. In addition, the fallbacks produced by the new `flexbox()` mixin (`-webkit-box`, `-moz-box`) make `.contents` a 2009-spec box container in legacy browsers, where `.title` and `.panel` will not behave like modern flex items; without the removed float, the layout in those legacy engines has no clear-float behavior. The change should at minimum be verified visually in a legacy-WebKit/Firefox fallback.
